Im Namen des souverainen Volks befehlen wir allen Munizipalitäten, vorstehendes Dekret in ihre Register einzuschreiben, verkündigen, anschlagen und als Landesgesetz vollstrecken zu lassen.
Mainz, den 27ten März 1793.
Die Mitglieder der allgemeinen provisorischen Administration. Dorsch, Präsident. Bleßmann, Sekretair.
units.en:
Decree of the Rhenish-German National Convention assembled at Mainz, of 27 March 1793, concerning the non-swearers, their families and goods.
The Rhenish-German National Convention, considering that its chief care must be to procure for the newly formed free state security against internal enemies as well; considering that all those are to be regarded as such who will not profess the principles of liberty and equality, these sole pillars of our free state, and refuse to take the oath prescribed for this purpose; considering finally that, since all means of mildness and indulgence are exhausted, measures of severity become necessary, decrees:
Art. 1. All those who do not take the prescribed citizens' oath within three days, counted from the day this decree is published, shall be taken out of the country together with their families.
Art. 2. In particular all persons of both sexes in public service, likewise all the privileged, as well as the widows and adult daughters of the former nobles, after first renouncing their privileges in writing, are bound to take this oath.
Art. 3. All persons who have so far resided in this country under the name of foreigners may remain in it if they take the prescribed oath and at the same time vouch for their quiet and peaceable character by the testimony and guarantee of 12 good citizens of their respective places of residence; otherwise they shall be expelled from the country without delay.
Art. 4. Those fit for labour and military service shall, after consultation with the Frankish national commissioners, be taken into the interior of France; the rest, however, across the Rhine.
Art. 5. Those proved to be agitators of the people shall be arrested immediately upon the proclamation of this decree, and once the term set above has expired, their deportation shall begin.
Art. 6. The movable and immovable property of those who have not yet taken the oath and still refuse to take it shall be seized at once; and if they let the three days allowed them pass still recalcitrant, they shall forfeit for ever not only their whole property but also all claims to citizenship.
Art. 7. The property of those proved to live in collusion with the enemies of our freedom, or to take an active part in their plans, is hereby declared forfeit to the state.
Art. 8. All those who conceal or remove any part of the property to be seized or confiscated under the present decree, or help to conceal or remove it, are to expect the penalty of confiscation of their own property.
Art. 9. The wife of a man to be deported who declares that she wishes to be divorced from her husband because he refuses to take the oath keeps the ownership and use of the property demonstrably due to her, but loses both as soon as it is proved that she is in collusion with her divorced husband or with enemies of the state in general.
Art. 10. The sons of the deported who are over 21 and have taken the citizens' oath, or will take it within the set time, keep the share of their parental property due to them.
Art. 11. Children from 14 to 21 years whose parents must be deported shall be permitted to remain in our state if they consent to it freely and are able to support themselves. The share of the inheritance due to them shall be handed over to them on coming of age, if they take the citizens' oath.
Art. 12. The National Convention will appoint special commissioners from its midst who, with the participation of the municipality, shall see to the execution of the present decree and report to the Convention on it.
Art. 13. The present decree shall at once be printed, sent to all municipalities, posted everywhere and solemnly proclaimed.
A. J. Hofmann, President. Frank, Gerhardi, Secretaries.
In the name of the sovereign people we order all municipalities to enter the above decree in their registers, to proclaim it, to post it and to have it executed as a law of the land.
Mainz, 27 March 1793.
The members of the general provisional administration. Dorsch, President. Blessmann, Secretary.
units.note: Das härteste Gesetz des Freistaats: drei Tage Frist, dann Ausweisung mit der Familie, Beschlag des Vermögens, Verlust des Bürgerrechts auf immer. Artikel 9 erlaubt der Frau, sich vom Nichtschwörer scheiden zu lassen, um ihr Vermögen zu behalten. Der Eid, im Februar Bedingung des Wahlrechts, ist im März Bedingung des Bleibens. Unterschrieben von Dorsch, dem Präsidenten der Administration, deren Vizepräsident Forster war.
units.note_en: The free state's harshest law: three days' grace, then expulsion with one's family, seizure of property, loss of citizenship for ever. Article 9 allows the wife to divorce the non-swearer in order to keep her property. The oath, in February the condition of the vote, is in March the condition of staying. Signed by Dorsch, president of the administration whose vice-president was Forster.
